title: What Is the Intel 14A PDK 0.9, and Why Does It Matter to Foundry Customers?
gist: Intel Foundry announced general availability of the Intel 14A PDK 0.9, which executives Ben Sell and Ali Farhang describe as silicon-validated, at industry-standard performance and yield maturity for this stage, and a gate many customers use to start designs. Intel 14A combines RibbonFET 2, PowerDirect backside power and Turbo Cells with Intel 18A learnings; EDA certifications from Cadence, Keysight, Siemens and Synopsys are in place and PDK 1.0 is expected in Q1 2027.

insights.claim: Intel Foundry announced general availability of the Intel 14A PDK 0.9, giving customers a more mature, silicon-validated design environment on the path to PDK 1.0 and high-volume manufacturing.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A tangible execution milestone for Intel's foundry turnaround.

insights.claim: Intel's Ben Sell says Intel 14A is reaching the industry-standard performance and yield maturity expected at the PDK 0.9 stage, supported by silicon-backed validation.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Management claims 14A is on schedule, relevant to Intel foundry customer wins.
insights.locator: From a customer perspective, the PDK 0.9

insights.claim: With PDK 0.9, customers can create designs that enter the fab for production around the time the process node is certified, and many customers use PDK 0.9 as a gate to start a design.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: PDK 0.9 availability could catalyse external 14A design starts, a leading indicator for foundry revenue.
insights.quote: The PDK 0.9 is an important proof point that many customers use as a gate to start a design.

insights.claim: Intel expects the Intel 14A PDK 1.0 in the first quarter of 2027.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Next checkpoint for tracking Intel 14A schedule credibility.
insights.quote: Our next major milestone is the Intel 14A PDK 1.0, expected in the first quarter of 2027.

insights.claim: Intel 14A builds on backside power delivery with PowerDirect and gate-all-around transistors with RibbonFET 2, adding Turbo Cells for flexibility in optimizing performance and efficiency.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Second-generation GAA plus backside power is Intel's leading-edge differentiation claim versus TSMC.

insights.claim: Intel 14A incorporates manufacturing learning from Intel 18A plus increased investment in inline detection, modeling and simulation to catch issues earlier.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: 18A learnings are claimed to de-risk 14A ramp.

insights.claim: Intel's Ali Farhang says that for fabless customers selecting a foundry is one of the most consequential decisions, so trust is paramount and PDK 0.9 demonstrates Intel Foundry can execute on commitments.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Intel frames schedule reliability as the core of its foundry pitch against TSMC.
insights.quote: In the foundry business, trust is paramount.

insights.claim: The PDK release lifecycle acts as the clock synchronizing internal R&D, EDA and IP partners, and customer design teams on a single shared schedule.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: PDK versions are useful milestones for tracking node readiness across the ecosystem.
insights.quote: the PDK release lifecycle serves as the clock that orchestrates technology development
insights.locator: Just as importantly, the PDK release

insights.claim: Cadence, Keysight, Siemens and Synopsys announced Intel 14A design-tool certifications earlier in 2026, and Cadence and Intel launched a DTCO collaboration to optimize 14A for AI-driven design tools and IP.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Full EDA vendor support removes a key barrier to external 14A adoption.

insights.claim: Intel has evolved its collaboration model with equipment and material suppliers, engaging them earlier and holding regular executive summits and engineering reviews to accelerate 14A progress.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Closer supplier engagement may speed node development.
